name: VoiceStudio
tagline: A local desktop application for voice cloning, dubbing, transcription, and audio production.
hook: Cross-platform parity means the same user-visible behavior, not the same hardware performance.
summary: VoiceStudio uses AGENTS.md as a compact operating contract and names CLAUDE.md as the fuller authority when the two conflict. The contract turns platform parity, offline testing, review handling, and local-first behavior into concrete checks while routing tracker and domain details to separate documents.

techniques.title: State the relationship between instruction files
techniques.body: The opening sentence identifies the audience of AGENTS.md and the role of CLAUDE.md. It also makes the project's intended precedence explicit instead of leaving the two files to appear interchangeable.
techniques.quote: Binding for every AI agent (Claude, Codex, Cursor, review bots, …). CLAUDE.md is the full constitution; this is the operating contract. When they conflict, CLAUDE.md wins.

techniques.title: Define parity in terms of what users can do
techniques.body: Hardware acceleration is allowed to vary by host. The guide distinguishes that from a missing user-visible feature and rejects disabling a working optimization everywhere as a way to satisfy parity.
techniques.quote:
- The parity rule covers user-visible BEHAVIOUR. Hardware acceleration varies by host by design (CUDA/MPS/DirectML, Triton availability, `torch.compile`); skipping an optimization where it physically cannot work is not a parity violation.
- Do not "fix" a parity finding by disabling a working optimization everywhere. That trades a real regression for a semantic one.
- A feature the user can see and use on one OS but not another IS a violation. Judge by what the user can do, not by how fast it runs.

techniques.title: Test offline behavior without a warm cache
techniques.body: The offline-test rule requires both an offline flag and an empty model cache. It names the reason: a populated development cache can hide the failure that CI will encounter.
techniques.quote: - Tests and CI simulate CI honestly: `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` + empty `HF_HUB_CACHE` — a populated dev cache masks real failures.

techniques.title: Give mechanical rules to deterministic checks
techniques.body: The file points at existing tests for changelog style, locale parity, version consistency, and CJK text. It directs the agent to read computed results before repeating their work.
techniques.quote: - Mechanical rules live in deterministic tests, never in agent effort: changelog style (`tests/test_changelog_style.py`), locale parity (`tests/test_locale_parity.py`), version lockstep (`tests/test_app_version.py`), CJK (`tests/test_no_hardcoded_cjk.py`).

techniques.title: Re-evaluate stale branches under current checks
techniques.body: The merge protocol warns that a green result from an older workflow is not evidence that current main will pass. It requires updating stale branches before evaluating their CI and watching the post-merge runs.
techniques.quote:
3. Merge current `main` into stale branches before judging their CI — PR-green under an old workflow ≠ main-green.
4. Gate: "Tests (backend + frontend)" green + MERGEABLE.
5. After EVERY merge: watch `main`'s own post-merge runs to green (`gh run list --branch main`). Red main = drop everything and fix.

techniques.title: Route synthetic audio through one boundary
techniques.body: The local-first rule bans new required network calls, gates model downloads, and names the shared synthetic-audio function. These are specific implementation boundaries for preserving the product promise.
techniques.quote: - Local-first: no new required network calls; any HF download gated on installed-ness or explicit user action; all synthetic audio through the `mark_synthetic` chokepoint.

steal: Describe how multiple instruction files relate and resolve conflicts.
Define cross-platform guarantees in observable behavior rather than machine speed.
Use empty caches when testing first-run and offline behavior.
Point mechanical checks at deterministic tests instead of asking agents to reproduce them.
Check integration results under the current workflow, not just an earlier branch snapshot.
outline: Change rules (see CLAUDE.md for full text)
